newsitem.title: USA: Minn. lawmakers approve flood repair spending plan.
newsitem.headline: Minn. lawmakers approve flood repair spending plan.

text.p: Minnesota lawmakers on Tuesday approved $124 million of state spending for repairs needed in the wake of widespread flooding last year, including $55.25 million of bonds.
House members voted 129-0 and Senators 65-0 to approve the spending plan, which will now be forwarded to Gov. Arne Carlson, legislative spokesmen said.
Carlson's spokeswoman Jackie Renner said the governor intends to sign the aid package, based on a task force he appointed to review the repair needs.
"The package is unprecedented and the governor knows that it won't meet everyone's needs, but it meets the most critical needs," Renner said.

A task force appointed by Carlson had recommended $123.98 million of state aid to repair damage from the widespread flooding in Minnesota last spring, including $55.25 million of bonds for various infrastructure repairs and the purchase of flood-damaged homes.

The borrowing plan includes $30 million of bonds to meet state and local matching requirements for public assistance through the Federal Emergency Management Agency. The proceeds would be used to leverage about $150 million of federal funding for infrastructure repair and replacement.
Another $5 million of bonds will go toward buying damaged houses in flood plains and another $5 million to finance floodproofing of public buildings and facilities.

Minnesota Housing Finance Authority will issue $7 million of bonds for water and sewer subsidies and the state will issue $3 million of bonds for a local matching program to construct ring dikes, provide emergency levee repairs and conduct future planning.
Another $4 million of bonds will go toward making grants and loans to local governments and $1.25 million of bonds for loans to farmers.
